title: Burst-Plateau Endurance & Autoscale Regression Harness
creator: Asha Menon
description: Build a repeatable, observable harness that validates Dedicated capacity behavior under an operational pattern we call 'burst-plateau': long steady-state request volume with intermittent short spikes. The goal is to measure tokens/sec throughput, p95 and p99 latency regressions, autoscaler responsiveness (time-to-scale and stability), and to detect regressions introduced by runtime/kernel changes or autoscaler tuning. This ticket delivers the harness, baseline artifacts, dashboards, and an automated regression job that runs nightly against a pinned baseline model and a quantized candidate variant.
background: Recent infra changes (kernel selection optimizations and batching heuristics) have improved average throughput but produced unexplained tail-latency variability in some Dedicated clusters. Existing soak tests either target pure steady-state or pure burst replay; they do not capture the interplay between a sustained plateau and frequent short bursts that many customers exercise (chat + background embeddings). We need a targeted harness that can reproduce that pattern deterministically and surface regressions via statistical tests and visual dashboards.
scenarios: Plateau-only: Ramp to target tokens/sec (T) over 5 minutes, hold for 2 hours; track p50/p95/p99, error rate, and KV cache hit ratio.
Burst-in-Plateau: Same plateau, with 60s bursts every 10 minutes at 3x T for 90s, then back to plateau. Repeat for 12 cycles to simulate daytime variability.
Sustained Burst Window: 10-minute sustained 2x T to validate autoscaler capacity during long surges.
Model-variant comparison: Run each scenario against baseline FP16 model and candidate int8-quantized model to detect latency/throughput regressions.
Failure-injection: Introduce delayed KV-store responses and transient GPU pod restarts to validate graceful degradation and fallback routing.
metrics_to_capture: autoscaler decision frequency and oscillation index
CPU/GPU utilization and scheduler queue length
cache hit ratio (prefix/KV) and token savings from caching
error rate (5xx), OOMs, and queue drops
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs unattended in CI against a dedicated ephemeral cluster and completes a full Burst-in-Plateau scenario within 3 hours
Nightly regression job compares candidate against baseline and fails the pipeline if p95 increases by >10% or tokens/sec drops by >7%
Dashboards (Console link) show token/sec, p95, autoscale events, and annotated burst windows; at least two slices (per-node and global) available
Regression detector produces a one-line summary and attaches a diff-of-curves artifact to the nightly run for triage
Automation includes optional failure-injection toggles and records deterministic seeds for replay
test_plan: Implement scenario generator in load-driver (internal loadgen) with deterministic seed and configurable user mix (chat/embeddings).
Wire metrics to Prometheus + Grafana and create Console view with alert rule templates for p95 and tokens/sec drifts.
Add model-variant runner that pins model revision and records model metadata (quantization, kernel profile).
Create regression job in CI that runs baseline vs candidate and uploads artifacts to S3; integrate with nightly pipeline.
Add lightweight statistical test (bootstrap on p95) to determine significance of regressions and avoid noisy alerts.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Ephemeral cluster limits may hide autoscaler edge cases. Mitigation: run one test on long-lived staging cluster monthly.
Risk: Statistical false positives from high variance workloads. Mitigation: use bootstrap + minimum-effect-size threshold and require repeatability across 3 runs before blocking release.
Risk: Nightly job cost. Mitigation: run full scenarios only on business nights; lightweight smoke checks on weekends.
next_steps: Finish PR feedback cycle and merge harness control plane into infratests main branch.
Coordinate with SRE to grant ephemeral cluster SA and add quota exemptions for nightly runs.
Finalize dashboard and alert thresholds, then onboard PM for acceptance testing with product traffic profiles.

notes: Keep scenario definitions parameterized so product teams can upload custom plateau/burst patterns for customer-incident repro. Where possible, reuse existing autoscaler telemetry instrumentation to avoid duplication.
